title: Bimodality of the elephant random walk: the bias interval, the threshold and rare reversals
author: Arjun Pemmasani
abstract:
We prove the conjecture of Gu\'erin, Laulin, Raschel and Simon that
the bimodal initial biases form a (possibly empty) open interval centered at one half
for each superdiffusive memory of the elephant random walk.
Outside this interval the limit density has one local maximum.
The interval is empty up to a unique memory threshold, which we
enclose near $0.6688128600146$. The fair density has two inflection
points below and at the threshold and four above it. At criticality
its maximum is quartic, the two modes emerge on a square-root
scale, and the bias interval opens on a three-halves scale.
Bimodality for memory at least $0.79$ has a proof
without computation. As memory tends to one, a two-component Landau
profile describes the density in total variation and scaled uniform
distance, uniformly over the initial bias.

For rare reversals, we give an explicit total variation approximation
by a truncated Luria--Delbr\"uck law and a Landau local limit theorem
with a rate. These bounds locate every mode. For even length $N$,
the origin and each end are equally likely at a unique reversal
probability, with $N\varepsilon=2\log N-\log\log N-\log16+o(1)$.
At this crossing every even $N\ge8$ has two symmetric modal plateaus
and a unique interior minimum.
